name: Taj Mahal
hint: A white marble mausoleum on the banks of the Yamuna river.
fact: Emperor Shah Jahan built it in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal; it was completed around 1653.

name: India Gate
hint: A 42 m war memorial at the end of Kartavya Path.
fact: Designed by Edwin Lutyens, it commemorates soldiers of the British Indian Army killed in World War I and the Third Anglo-Afghan War.

name: Gateway of India
hint: A basalt arch facing the Arabian Sea in India's financial capital.
fact: It was built to mark the 1911 visit of King George V and Queen Mary, and was completed in 1924.

name: Hawa Mahal
hint: A pink sandstone palace front shaped like a honeycomb.
fact: Built in 1799, its 953 small windows let royal women watch street life without being seen.

name: Charminar
hint: A square monument with four slender minarets, surrounded by bustling bazaars.
fact: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, founder of the city, built it in 1591.

name: Victoria Memorial
hint: A grand white marble museum set in landscaped gardens in a former capital.
fact: Built between 1906 and 1921 from white Makrana marble, it is dedicated to Queen Victoria.

name: Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib)
hint: A gold-covered Sikh shrine floating in the middle of a sacred pool.
fact: Its community kitchen (langar) serves free meals to tens of thousands of visitors every day.

name: Qutub Minar
hint: A tall red sandstone victory tower with a famous rust-free iron pillar nearby.
fact: At about 73 m it is among the tallest brick minarets in the world; construction began in 1192.

name: Mysore Palace
hint: The Wadiyar dynasty's royal residence, famous for Dasara celebrations.
fact: Rebuilt after a fire and finished in 1912, it is lit by nearly 100,000 bulbs on Sundays and festival days.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
hint: A Dravidian temple complex with colourful towers covered in sculpted figures.
fact: The complex has around 14 gateway towers (gopurams), each covered with thousands of painted stucco figures.

name: Konark Sun Temple
hint: A temple designed as a giant stone chariot, close to the Bay of Bengal coast.
fact: Built in the 13th century, its 24 carved wheels double as sundials that can tell the time.

name: Stone Chariot, Vittala Temple (Hampi)
hint: A stone shrine shaped like a chariot, among boulder-strewn ruins of an old empire.
fact: Part of the 16th-century Vijayanagara capital ruins, it appears on the Indian 50-rupee note.

name: Ajanta Caves
hint: Horseshoe-shaped cliff with rock-cut Buddhist monasteries and ancient murals.
fact: About 30 caves were carved between roughly the 2nd century BCE and 480 CE, and were rediscovered by a British officer on a tiger hunt in 1819.

name: Sanchi Stupa
hint: A hemispherical Buddhist dome on a hilltop, with four intricately carved gateways.
fact: Commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, it is one of the oldest stone structures in India.

name: Double-Decker Living Root Bridge
hint: A bridge grown, not built, from tree roots in one of the wettest regions on Earth.
fact: The Khasi people guide rubber fig roots across streams; a bridge can take 15 years or more to become usable and some are centuries old.

name: Red Fort
hint: A massive red sandstone fortress whose ramparts host a national flag-hoisting every August.
fact: Built by Shah Jahan between 1638 and 1648, it is where India's Prime Minister addresses the nation on Independence Day.

name: Lotus Temple
hint: A modern house of worship shaped like a half-opened flower, surrounded by pools.
fact: Completed in 1986, this Bahai House of Worship has 27 free-standing marble-clad petals and welcomes people of all faiths.

name: Humayun's Tomb
hint: A red sandstone and white marble garden tomb that inspired a more famous monument.
fact: Built from 1565 to 1572 and commissioned by Humayun's widow Bega Begum, it was the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent.

name: Jama Masjid, Delhi
hint: One of India's largest mosques, facing a historic fort across a busy old-city road.
fact: Commissioned by Shah Jahan and completed in 1656, its courtyard can hold around 25,000 worshippers.

name: Agra Fort
hint: A red sandstone Mughal fortress with a famous white marble monument visible from its walls.
fact: Akbar began building it in 1565, and Shah Jahan spent his last years confined here, gazing towards the Taj Mahal.

name: Fatehpur Sikri (Buland Darwaza)
hint: A huge sandstone gateway at an abandoned Mughal capital city.
fact: Akbar built this capital in the 1570s but it was left within about 14 years; its Buland Darwaza gateway is roughly 54 m high.

name: Amber Fort
hint: A hilltop fort-palace above a lake, once reached by elephant rides.
fact: Raja Man Singh I began building it in 1592, and its Sheesh Mahal is decorated with thousands of tiny mirrors.

name: City Palace, Udaipur
hint: A sprawling palace complex rising straight from the shore of a lake in the 'City of Lakes'.
fact: Founded by Maharana Udai Singh II in 1553, it was extended by successive rulers over roughly 400 years.

name: Mehrangarh Fort
hint: A mighty fort on a steep rock above a city famous for its blue-painted houses.
fact: Rao Jodha founded it in 1459, and its walls rise more than 100 m above the surrounding old city.

name: Jaisalmer Fort
hint: A honey-coloured sandstone fort rising from the Thar Desert.
fact: Built in 1156 by Rawal Jaisal, it is one of the few 'living forts' in the world, with people still residing inside.

name: Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
hint: An open-air observatory of giant geometric stone instruments.
fact: Built by Maharaja Jai Singh II in the 1720s-30s, it holds the Samrat Yantra, among the largest stone sundials in the world.

name: Dashashwamedh Ghat, Varanasi
hint: Stone steps leading down to a sacred river, famous for an evening fire ceremony.
fact: Varanasi is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, and the evening Ganga aarti is held at this ghat.

name: Khajuraho Temples (Kandariya Mahadeva)
hint: Medieval sandstone temples with towering spires and densely sculpted walls.
fact: The Chandela dynasty built most of these temples between about 950 and 1050 CE, and they are famed for their detailed sculpture.

name: Dal Lake, Srinagar
hint: A mountain-ringed lake with houseboats and small paddled boats called shikaras.
fact: Dal Lake is known for its floating gardens and a floating vegetable market held early in the morning.

name: Pangong Tso
hint: A long, deep-blue high-altitude lake in a cold desert, shared with a neighbouring country.
fact: At about 4,350 m above sea level, this brackish lake stretches across the India-China border.

name: Valley of Flowers
hint: A high-altitude Himalayan meadow carpeted with wildflowers in the monsoon.
fact: This Uttarakhand national park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is home to hundreds of species of alpine flowers.

name: Gol Gumbaz
hint: A mausoleum with one of the largest domes in the world and a famous whispering gallery.
fact: Completed in 1656 as the tomb of Sultan Muhammad Adil Shah, its gallery carries even a whisper across the dome.

name: Brihadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur
hint: A granite Chola temple with a towering pyramidal vimana and a giant stone bull.
fact: Completed in 1010 CE by Rajaraja Chola I, its main tower rises about 66 m and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Shore Temple, Mahabalipuram
hint: A weathered granite temple standing right on the Bay of Bengal coast.
fact: Built in the 8th century by the Pallava dynasty, it is among the oldest structural stone temples in South India.

name: Vivekananda Rock Memorial, Kanyakumari
hint: A memorial on a rock island off the southernmost tip of the mainland.
fact: Completed in 1970, it stands where the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal and the Indian Ocean meet.

name: Munnar Tea Gardens
hint: Rolling green hills striped with tea bushes in the Western Ghats.
fact: The Neelakurinji flower blooms in the hills around here only once every 12 years, painting the slopes blue.

name: Alleppey Backwaters
hint: A maze of palm-fringed canals and lagoons, explored on traditional houseboats.
fact: The houseboats here are converted kettuvallam, traditional rice-carrying barges built without nails.

name: Golconda Fort
hint: A ruined granite hill fort west of a city known for pearls and biryani.
fact: A hand clap at its grand entrance can reportedly be heard at the hilltop pavilion, an ancient alarm system.

name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
hint: A laterite-stone baroque church in a former Portuguese colonial capital.
fact: Completed in 1605, it holds the remains of St Francis Xavier and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Elephanta Caves
hint: Rock-cut cave temples with a huge three-faced Shiva sculpture, reached by ferry.
fact: Carved on an island in Mumbai harbour roughly between the 5th and 8th centuries, they are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Kailasa Temple, Ellora
hint: An entire temple complex carved from a single rock face.
fact: Built in the 8th century by the Rashtrakuta dynasty, it was carved from the top down out of one massive rock.

name: Statue of Unity
hint: A colossal bronze-clad statue of a freedom-movement leader beside a river dam.
fact: At 182 m, it was inaugurated in 2018 as the tallest statue in the world and honours Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

name: Rani ki Vav, Patan
hint: An underground stepwell with seven levels of finely carved sculptures.
fact: Built in the 11th century, this UNESCO stepwell is featured on the Indian 100-rupee note.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
hint: A Victorian Gothic railway station with domes, turrets and stained glass.
fact: Completed in 1888 and once called Victoria Terminus, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and still a busy station.

name: Howrah Bridge
hint: A giant steel cantilever bridge over the Hooghly river, crowded with traffic and pedestrians.
fact: Opened in 1943, it was built with rivets instead of nuts and bolts and carries an enormous amount of daily traffic.

name: Jagannath Temple, Puri
hint: A towering Kalinga-style temple of a famous annual chariot festival, near a beach town.
fact: Each year, the Rath Yatra festival sees enormous wooden chariots pulled through the streets by thousands of devotees.

name: Mahabodhi Temple, Bodh Gaya
hint: A pyramidal brick temple beside a sacred fig tree, a major Buddhist pilgrimage site.
fact: This UNESCO site marks the place where the Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment under a Bodhi tree.

name: Kaziranga National Park
hint: Tall elephant-grass wetlands beside a big river, home to a famous armoured herbivore.
fact: This UNESCO park shelters about two-thirds of the world's population of one-horned rhinoceroses.

name: Tawang Monastery
hint: A huge hilltop Buddhist monastery in the high Himalayas near an international border.
fact: Founded in the 17th century, it is the largest monastery in India and one of the biggest in the world.

name: Cellular Jail, Port Blair
hint: A red-brick colonial prison with radiating wings, on a remote island chain.
fact: Built by the British between 1896 and 1906, it held freedom fighters and was nicknamed 'Kala Pani'.
